InlandWaterways.Summary: Comfortable for inland cruising, but beam, air draft and fuel consumption must be checked against route and marina constraints.

ExposedWater.Summary: These are coastal production cruisers; actual capability depends on generation, loading, machinery, weather and individual condition.

TradeOffs: Twin gasoline inboards increase fuel and maintenance cost
Flybridge height and windage affect route and docking considerations
Condition and refit history matter substantially on older examples
BestFor: Coastal and Great Lakes cruising
Owners wanting sedan accommodation with a flybridge
Light fishing and family cruising
InspectionFocus: Inspect deck, flybridge and window penetrations for moisture
Inspect fuel tanks, exhaust, cooling, wiring and steering
Verify engines, transmissions, shafts, struts and rudders
Confirm model year against generation-specific dimensions and tankage
BuyerQuestions: Which generation and model year is the boat?
Which original or replacement engines are installed?
What tank, structural, deck or window repairs have been completed?
Are flybridge, hardtop or enclosure modifications original?
OwnerActions: Maintain deck, window and hardware seals
Maintain fuel, exhaust, cooling, steering and electrical systems
Document repowers and major structural or tank work
